senses.d: An expression of mirth particular to the human species; the sound heard in laughing; laughter.
ex: His deep laughs boomed through the room.
And the loud laugh that spoke the vacant mind.

senses.d: Something that provokes mirth or scorn.
ex: Your new hat's an absolute laugh, dude.
Life's a piece of shit / When you look at it / Life's a laugh and death's a joke, it's true.

senses.d: A fun person.
ex: a good laugh

senses.d: To show mirth, satisfaction, or derision, by peculiar movement of the muscles of the face, particularly of the mouth, causing a lighting up of the face and eyes, and usually accompanied by the emission of explosive or chuckling sounds from the chest and throat; to indulge in laughter.
ex: There were many laughing children running on the school grounds.
But there was ſuch laughing, Queen Hecuba laught that her eyes ran ore.

senses.d: To be or appear cheerful, pleasant, mirthful, lively, or brilliant; to sparkle; to sport.
ex: In Folly’s Cup ſtill laughs the Bubble, Joy; [...]

senses.d: To make an object of laughter or ridicule; to make fun of; to deride; to mock.
ex: Don't laugh at my new hat, man!
On the corner is a banker with a motorcar / The little children laugh at him behind his back

senses.d: To affect or influence by means of laughter or ridicule.
ex: Will you laugh me aſleepe, for I am very heauy.

senses.d: To express by, or utter with, laughter.
ex: From his deepe cheſt laughes out a lowd applauſe, [...]
Fairfax addressed her as "my lady," she laughed her musical laugh, and glanced up at a picture of Gerald with eyes full of exultation.
